limits.severity: low, outside the letter of criterion 1
limits.measured: AITELIER_DSH_TEST_ENTRY pointing at a path that does not exist (a typo, or an uninstalled build) or at a directory does NOT refuse: status 'measured', source 'host install', measuredEntryForTest returned the host binary. The only trace is the diagnostic 'measuring @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.1-rc.5 (host install): ...', i.e. a source the caller did not ask for. So 'an explicit override names the binary the run must measure' is enforced for wrong-version and unattributable overrides (both measured as refusing, walk stopped) but not for an override that is not a regular file. A test run with a mistyped override therefore measures the implicit install and is green.

A file that is not dsh but sits inside the pinned package directory (…/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/rogue-review-probe.js) is attributed to 0.2.1-rc.5 and 'measured'. The resolver never checks the binary is the package's declared bin. Strictly the criterion is about the resolved package's version and that package is pinned, so this is a limit rather than a failure; the probe file was deleted immediately (verified absent).

runtime.smoke.test.mjs alone cannot detect a resolver regression: with M2 (explicit override routed around, the historic bug) it is green (exit 0, 2 pass) while measuring the host install, and with M8 (always unmeasured) it is exit 0 with 2 skips. dsh-entry.test.mjs catches both (M2: exactly 1 fail; M8: 3 fails). Also, runtime.smoke.test.mjs itself contains no assertion that it was not skipped when an install exists. Keeping dsh-entry.test.mjs in the same gate as runtime.smoke.test.mjs is therefore load-bearing, not optional.

A clean `node --test dsh-entry.test.mjs` run created 0 new /tmp/dsh-entry-* directories (fixtures are removed by each test's trailing rm). Failing mutant runs abort at their assertion before the rm, so they leave /tmp/dsh-entry-* fixtures behind; the 41 such directories present during this review (from mutant runs, mine and earlier ones) were removed afterwards, my own /tmp/dsh-review-* fixtures too.
